title: Gate review 1:1 action tracker (pre-release)
content:
Purpose: quick personal prep + running log for the 1:1 with Jonas (release lead) tomorrow. Use this to drive the go/no-go decision conversation and capture owners/next steps. Informal notes — will clean up after meeting for the weekly ops doc.

Meeting context:
- Release train window: 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-22 (soft launch 3/17)
- This 1:1 is a tactical gate review: verify blockers, confirm rollback plan, owners for last-mile tasks.
- Primary ask from PMs: ensure canary pass by EOD 3/16, otherwise gate to postpone.

Quick agenda (10–15m):
1) Current red/amber/green list (top 6) — 5m
2) Go/no-go criteria alignment — 3m
3) Assignment of immediate actions + deadlines — 5m
4) Confirm comms/owner for rollback and postmort plan — 2m

Top items snapshot (my quick status notes):
1) Canary environment stability — STATUS: AMBER
   - Symptom: intermittent OOM alerts on p3a-16x w/ batching=8 (see ENGINF-2387).
   - Owner: Priya (infra) — action: reduce default batch size to 4 for canary, monitor 1 hour.
   - Due: 2026-03-12 17:00 PDT.
   - Mitigation if persists: revert to smaller instance type + lower qps routing (backup config in REL-421).

2) Model artifact checksum mismatch during canary rollout — STATUS: GREEN (fixed)
   - Root cause: packaging script edge-case; PR merged (serving-runtime #1284).
   - Owner: Ethan — validate artifact hashes across all zones before canary start.
   - Follow-up: smoke test report uploaded to Confluence page.

3) Metrics pipeline lag (latency dashboards delayed 15–30m) — STATUS: AMBER
   - Impact: slower detection of regressions during canary.
   - Owner: Jonas (telemetry) — action: enable immediate push for critical histograms (temp).
   - Due: 2026-03-12 16:30 PDT.

4) Canary user routing rules (feature flag) — STATUS: GREEN
   - Validation: flags reviewed; rollout targeting correct hosts.
   - Owner: Maya (me) — confirm 5 test sessions from QA before canary.

5) Compliance review (data residency + KMS) — STATUS: GREEN
   - Docs approved for this release; audit log config verified.
   - Owner: Priya to confirm final KMS rotation window not overlapping launch.

6) Load testing (95th + p95 latency under spike) — STATUS: RED
   - Current: p95 breaches target under synthetic spike scenario 3.
   - Owner: Ethan & infra — options: postpone spike test until after canary OR increase canary capacity for spike window.
   - Decision needed in 1:1: do we accept elevated p95 for soft launch? (likely no.)

Go / No-go quick checklist (talking points + acceptance criteria):
- Canary health: no persistent OOMs for 60 minutes after batching change (owner: Priya) — ACCEPT if pass.
- Artifact consistency: all zones show matching checksums and image tags (owner: Ethan) — ACCEPT if verified.
- Telemetry latency <= 5m for critical metrics (owner: Jonas) — ACCEPT if improved.
- No open severity-1 issues in the last 24 hours (owner: release-team) — ACCEPT if none.
- Rollback plan validated and owner assigned (owner: Maya) — ACCEPT if documented & contactable.
- Spike test result: p95 <= target OR documented mitigation/temporary throttle plan (owner: Ethan) — ACCEPT if mitigation approved.

If any of the above fail -> HOLD the push, immediate action plan + next checkpoint time (recommend 4 hours).

Rollback / Backout notes (short):
- Primary rollback: revert traffic routing to baseline config (Route ID: rt-main-2026-03). Steps in REL-421 runbook.
- Fallback model: quantized-medium variant in the fallback pool if OOMs occur (owner: Priya).
- Communication: policy: #launch-week Slack + alert to SRE on-call and product PMs.

Owners & immediate actions to confirm in 1:1 (my proposed assignments):
- Priya: reduce batch size & watch canary (due 3/12 17:00) — if green, escalate to full canary on 3/16.
- Ethan: validate artifact checksums across zones; run smoke harness (due 3/12 18:00).
- Jonas: push temp metrics flush for critical histos (due 3/12 16:30); confirm dashboard refresh.
- Maya (me): validate feature flag targeting + be primary comms lead for rollback; create short post-launch checklist doc (due 3/13 09:00).
- QA (TBD): run 5 manual sessions and confirm expected responses (owner: QA lead, request via REL-421).

Notes-to-self / expected friction during 1:1:
- Keep conversation tight — focus on top 3 blockers only.
- Ask Jonas for tradeoff: accept softer p95 with mitigations vs delay. Capture his raw read.
- If Priya says OOMs still happen after batch reduction, ask for immediate capacity increase plan and cost acknowledgement.

Open questions to surface:
- Do we have a go/no-go committee signoff process documented for post-3/16 escalations? (I think yes but verify Confluence link.)
- If telemetry lag remains, can we rely on passive alarms rather than live dashboards? What thresholds are safe?
- Who explicitly owns customer comms in case of a rollback after hours? (Need primary + backup).

Post-meeting follow-up template (I'll use this to update the shared weekly doc):
- Decision: GO / HOLD / ROLLBACK (explicit timestamp + owner).
- Why: short rationale (3 bullets).
- Actions assigned (owner, desc, due).
- Next checkpoint time.
- Slack summary (1–2 lines) + recipients list.

Misc small reminders: attach REL-421 to the meeting invite, ping QA lead in Slack before 1:1.

Bottom line (my current stance going into 1:1):
- Leaning HOLD if spike test remains RED; otherwise can proceed with cautious canary if Priya's OOM mitigation stabilizes and Jonas shortens telemetry lag.

End of scratchpad — convert into formal note after 1:1.
